plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to zero.
Exit high-beta software (METU, PLTU) to reduce risk.
Trim income ETF (QQQI) to 20% to lower concentration.
Buy inverse ETF (TECS) for market hedging.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation with reduced leverage.
Expect a lower target return with a focus on minimizing drawdowns.
conservative.read: This plan aims for capital preservation with a target of around 1.5% per month. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, holding a larger cash buffer. Expect lower potential gains but also a more stable ride with reduced drawdown risk.

plan: Reduce leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to minimal levels.
Trim high-beta software (METU, PLTU) to reduce concentration.
Trim income ETF (QQQI) to 20% for better diversification.
Buy inverse ETF (TECS) to add a defensive hedge.
This plan balances risk reduction with continued growth potential.
Expect a moderate target return with controlled drawdowns.
balanced.read: This balanced approach targets around 2.5% per month by reducing leverage and concentration while adding a defensive hedge. It aims for risk-first growth, blending broad market exposure with quality tech and a small allocation to leveraged plays. Drawdowns are expected to be moderate.

plan: Increase leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to capitalize on potential upside.
Add to high-beta software (METU, PLTU) for concentrated growth.
Trim income ETF (QQQI) to 15% to free up capital for growth.
Buy inverse ETF (TECS) to provide a hedge against market downturns.
This plan aggressively pursues growth through concentration and leverage.
Expect higher potential returns but also significantly larger drawdowns and leverage decay.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month by leaning into leveraged ETFs and concentrated high-beta tech, with a smaller cash buffer. It accepts higher risk for potentially higher rewards. Be aware of amplified drawdowns, leverage decay in ETFs, and the need for strict stop discipline.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs and high-beta software to zero.
Increase allocation to income ETF (QQQI) to 30% for yield.
Trim broad index (SPY) to 10% to prioritize income generation.
This plan focuses on generating steady monthly income.
Expect low drawdowns and consistent, though variable, distributions.
Growth potential is secondary to capital preservation and income.
income.read: This income-focused plan targets around 1% per month by prioritizing income-generating ETFs and reducing volatile assets. It aims for low drawdowns and reliable monthly distributions, not aggressive growth. NAV can still decline in market selloffs, so it's not a savings account.
